q1: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) >1
q2: SELECT DISTINCT P.EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON P JOIN PERSON Q ON P.EMAIL = Q.EMAIL WHERE P.ID != Q.ID
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT EMAIL AS EMAIL FROM PERSON GROUP BY EMAIL HAVING COUNT(EMAIL) >1

explanation: Q1 groups the records by email and checks if the count of emails is greater than 1, which will return all emails that appear more than once in the table. Q2, on the other hand, finds distinct emails where there are at least two different IDs associated with the same email, which means it's looking for duplicate emails in terms of user IDs.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have at least one email that appears more than once with different IDs, and another email that appears only once.
